findings.F1: The tested idea dropped the brief's calm-market restriction, and its result is diluted by that. On the 5-day grid in folds B–C, up days in calm markets have a graded slope of the unusual move on the day's size in swing units of +0.024 (t 2.75, 305 cases) and a mean unusual move of +1.48 % (day-pooled t 1.38, strength 0.12). Up days in agitated markets have a slope of +0.010 (t 0.79, 280 cases) and a mean of +0.46 % (t 0.40, strength 0.03).
findings.F2: The step-5 cases have the sign the idea predicts in calm markets and the opposite sign in agitated ones. Replicated in folds B–C, calm cases average +0.12 % (t 0.29, 545 cases) and agitated cases −0.53 % (t −1.02, 551). Choppy agitated cases alone fall −4.2 % (t −3.11, 31).
findings.F3: The effect is clearest in rising calm markets and absent or reversed in falling ones. Step-5 cases in rising calm markets average +1.83 % (t 2.19, 162 cases) against −2.22 % in falling calm (t −2.32, 116). On the grid, calm up days in a rising trend average +4.23 % (day-pooled t 1.92, strength 0.35, 94 cases) against −0.23 % in a falling trend (t −0.13, 71).
findings.F4: The overall mean is pulled below zero by the small and middling forecasts, while the largest ones go the predicted way. The two lower forecast quartiles average −1.50 % (t −2.80) and −1.68 % (t −2.78), the top quartile +1.17 % (t 1.69), 371 cases each. Calm grid up days above 2 swing units average +7.9 % (day-pooled t 1.66, strength 0.59, 24 cases).
findings.F5: The effect shifts with the period. Step-5 cases average −3.04 % in 2018 (t −4.31) and +1.12 % in 2020 (t 2.27). Calm grid up days are negative in 2018 (−4.4 %, t −1.52) and positive in 2019–2021 (+1.5 %, +2.1 %, +4.9 %; t up to 2.08). Most of the market's own moves land on the calm up days of a falling year.
findings.F6: Calm down days show no mirror continuation. Their unusual move is −0.89 % (day-pooled t −1.18, 335 cases) and the graded slope +0.007 (t 0.84), so the long-only side the test chose is the right one.

ideas.idea: In a calm market, the larger a coin's one-day rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the further it keeps rising over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader follows large up days on the long side only while the coin's swing is at or below its usual level, sized by the day's size in swing units, and ignores large up days in agitated markets.
ideas.name: calm big up-day continues

ideas.idea: In a rising, calm market, the larger a coin's one-day rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the further it keeps rising over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader follows large up days on the long side only when the coin has been rising over the past two months on quiet swings, sized by the day's size in swing units.
ideas.name: rising calm up-day continuation
